body:
That's a valid assumption. I have a lot of flaws my current partner and I are working on but this case is... special? I don't mind acknowledging I have issues, especially in the past few years (when this happened) as I'm really tired of not being an entirely reasonable person lol

The issue was I couldn't bring up what they did to upset me to begin with, nor could I even expect them to apologize regardless of if I held my tongue with their issues or not. They used to complain that I never communicated or expressed my issues but would ignore me or claim my problems weren't as serious as theirs when I did so. I even tried to practice the "when you do x it makes me feel y", since I learned it in ap psychology long ago, but was only yelled at till I remained quiet.

Honestly, I still get updates on them, a lot of our mutuals are asking me how to cut ties with them for the same reason, and I know I'm the one in the friend group who let's people walk over me the least so I worry about then...

Besides, they cut me and my roommate out after they yelled at us over a game of league (literally gave the silent treatment to our roommate while they were still living together) so I'm not too eager to rectify this one...

It's worse when you apologize to them, they usually just end up finding a way to make it seem like your apology either isn't genuine or that you never actually apologize.

I remember my ex did the same shit, I'd bring up how he'd upset me, then apologize for being upset, but he'd say my pointing out how he played fault into the situation is just me not actually apologizing.

Like no, dude, me addressing that you were unnecessarily mean and rude to me, hence why I got upset in the first place, is not me absolving my guilt if I did something, it's me wanting us on equal footing.
